change: the gradebook rollup, at every level above the student row: points, not a mean of percentages, and three denominators that are three different numbers
_context: Board 85. Its headline half was fixed on 2026-09-02: a student's overall grade has
summed points since then, and the run note from 2026-09-03 checked that and said so.
What nobody compared was every OTHER number on the same page, and five of them kept
the old arithmetic with every gradebook suite in this repo green:
the lesson cell     printed '10 / 30' with '60%' beside it. The pair summed marks,
the percent averaged the two item percentages, and nothing
required them to agree. Ten marks out of thirty is 33.
the column footer   class average per assignment, a mean over students
the lesson footer   the same, per lesson
the activity rollup a mean of column averages, weighted by heads not marks
the class average   a mean of student percentages, so a student on 1 / 1 weighed
the same as a student on 12 / 40
That is the same sentence board 85 is written in, one level up: a 5 point quiz
weighing the same as a 25 point project. It is also what the 2026-09-11 percent fix
left open, in its own words, and handed back to 85.
And one denominator too many was collapsed. overall.possible carried the ATTEMPTED
sum, which docs/gradebook-contract.md calls `graded`, so a consumer asking how much
of the course is priced got a number equal to the graded total by construction and
therefore always reading as complete. The course total was not reported at all.
Found on the way: public/teachers.html has drawn a lost-score X from cell.score_missing
and a legend from overall.items_score_missing since the contract landed. This builder
set neither, so both were dead code on the operator page and a graded activity
finished with no score rendered as 'done', which reads as done and fine.

checks.name: every level rolls up marks, on a fixture where the two rules give different answers
checks._why: smoke/admin-gradebook.js stayed green through all of this because its columns are equally weighted, and where every cell in a column is out of the same number a mean of percentages and a points average ARE the same number. No assertion over that fixture could tell the two rules apart. This one is built so they differ at every level. Measured against the pre-fix builder: 35 of its 47 assertions fail, including the lesson cell reading 60 beside '10 / 30', the column footer reading 70 instead of 86, and the class average reading 74 instead of 63.

checks.name: a second implementation reaches the same rollup from the raw rows
checks._why: Reads progress, attempts, course_denominators and course_manifest with plain SELECTs, groups them in JavaScript, and imports nothing from either builder: not the grid, not pointsFromRatio, not gradePct. Cells are generated across the axes that decide the answer (which pipeline wrote the cell, whether an out-of was authored, whether the page reported its own, how heavy the column is, whether the student finished it with no score) and the fixture is asserted to be thick enough to prove something before a pass is reported. Against the pre-fix builder on seed 20260911 it reports 69 disagreements out of 153 numbers compared, so it is not hollow.
checks.expect: OK - the builder and the rederivation agree

checks.name: the full battery, twelve mutations, each on its own named assertion
checks._why: Six places apply this arithmetic and any one can rot while the other five hold, which is precisely what happened. A mutation that reddens the suite SOMEWHERE ELSE certifies a level nothing tested, so every entry names the assertion it has to break, an anchor that stops matching is itself a failure, and the battery refuses to report anything if the baseline is not green first.
